records.summary: 659 Columbus Ave operates as Piazza Pellegrini, a full-service restaurant with an active Type 47 liquor license that has been continuously permitted since 1995. The site history shows three prior Conditional Use Authorizations: the original 1,000 sq ft restaurant in 1995, expansion to over 2,000 sq ft in 2009, and addition of a full bar in 2003. The North Beach Special Use District rule at Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) explicitly prohibits a restaurant from enlarging its existing space, which the pathway analysis confirms makes this proposed 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft expansion "not permitted" even though the restaurant use itself continues. The immediate area is densely packed with 20 food/drink businesses and 11 on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 42 licenses within 1,000 ft.

patterns.pattern: All 19 Planning actions for restaurants in the North Beach NCD within 500 ft since 2019 were approved. However, 17 of 19 were agency referrals (ABC license reviews, DPH health permits) labeled as continuation of existing use, not use decisions requiring Commission hearings.

Only two use decisions requiring Commission hearings appear in the North Beach NCD candidates since 2015: the 2019-013418CUA adding a full kitchen (approved June 2020 after 11 months) and the 2015-014178CUA upgrading a liquor license (approved March 2016 after 4.5 months). Both were approved with standard restaurant operating conditions.

Restaurant CUAs approved in the North Beach NCD imposed standard operating conditions: odor control equipment, noise insulation, sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius, garbage kept indoors, and appointment of a community liaison officer.

Special legislation in 2020 (Ordinance 182-20) temporarily allowed Limited Restaurants in the North Beach SUD to convert to full Restaurants without CUA if they operated as bona fide eating places for three years. This temporary pathway expired and does not apply to physical expansions.

ABC license transfers and upgrades at existing North Beach restaurants have been routinely approved as continuation of use, including Type 41 beer-and-wine and Type 47 full-bar licenses, when the restaurant space itself is not being enlarged.

risk.concept_summary: A restaurant at 659 Columbus Ave in the North Beach NCD seeks to expand from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft with tenant improvements, limited cooking, no alcohol service, and recorded music.

overall.next_step: Request a written Letter of Determination from San Francisco Planning to confirm whether Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits this expansion, and whether any variance or exception pathway exists, before signing the lease or filing any application.

approvals.summary: A Conditional Use Authorization is needed because the restaurant is over 2,000 sq ft and is enlarging a nonconforming use, but the North Beach Special Use District rule at §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits enlarging an existing restaurant space, so the status is further review.

findings.text: An active Type 47 on-sale general eating-place license has been on file at 659 Columbus Ave since May 2021, indicating the space operates as a restaurant.

Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) provides that a new restaurant in the North Beach Special Use District may be approved by Conditional Use on the first story only if the Zoning Administrator first finds the space is currently or was last legally occupied by a restaurant or bar, that use was not discontinued or abandoned, and the new restaurant will not enlarge the space.
The concept proposes to increase the floor area from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft, which is an enlargement, so the condition that the new restaurant will not enlarge the space is not met.

Three prior Conditional Use Authorizations are on file at this address: the original 1,000 sq ft restaurant approved in August 1995, expansion to over 2,000 sq ft approved in February 2010, and addition of a full bar approved in December 2003.

The 2010 Conditional Use Authorization (case 2009.0798C) approved expansion of the full-service restaurant for use size over 2,000 sq ft, demonstrating that a prior enlargement was authorized under the North Beach rules as they stood in 2010.

No conditions text is available for the 2009 or 2003 CUAs, and no record in the candidate set since 2010 shows a restaurant square-footage expansion approved in the North Beach Special Use District, so whether current Planning practice permits enlargement despite §780.3(c)(1)(B) is not established.

approvals.summary: A health permit to operate is allowed for a food facility with limited cooking; it is issued after plan check and inspection without a discretionary hearing.

findings.text: California Retail Food Code §§114380–114381 and San Francisco Health Code Article 8 require a health permit to operate for any food or drink business, issued after plan check and inspection.
The health permit application is sent to the Planning Department for a zoning review referral, which is a review step inside the health permit approval, not a separate approval.

approvals.summary: A building permit is needed for tenant improvements, but whether a change of occupancy is required is insufficient information because the number of occupants and the existing occupancy group are not known.

findings.text: The California Building Code classifies a restaurant or bar as Assembly Group A-2, and a space for fewer than 50 people as Group B, so the proposed occupancy group depends on the number of occupants.
The description does not state whether the space is for fewer than 50 people, so the proposed occupancy group is not established.
The existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show it, so a change of occupancy is not established.
San Francisco Building Code §106A.1 requires a building permit for tenant improvements, alterations, and any change of occupancy, with fees based on a percentage of construction valuation.

expected_conditions.condition: The authorization is valid for three years; a building permit must be issued and construction commenced within that period or the authorization lapses.
expected_conditions.basis: This is a standard condition in every San Francisco Planning Commission CUA. The 2019 CUA at 526 Columbus (case 2019-013418CUA) included validity, expiration, and diligent pursuit conditions requiring a building permit within three years and continuous construction to completion.

expected_conditions.condition: Odor control equipment must be installed, maintained, and shown on building permit plans to prevent noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises; odor control ducting shall not be applied to the primary façade.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019 CUA at 526 Columbus required odor control equipment details and manufacturer specifications on the building permit plans, and prohibited ducting on the primary façade. This is standard for restaurant CUAs with cooking.

expected_conditions.condition: The premises shall be soundproofed or insulated so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises or in other sections of the building, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels in the San Francisco Noise Control Ordinance.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019 CUA at 526 Columbus imposed this noise condition. It is standard for eating and drinking uses in dense residential areas like North Beach.

expected_conditions.condition: The operator shall maintain the main entrance and all sidewalks abutting the property in a clean and sanitary condition, and shall daily monitor the sidewalk within a one-block radius to keep it free of litter associated with the business during business hours.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019 CUA at 526 Columbus included this sidewalk maintenance condition in compliance with San Francisco Police Code Article 1, Section 34. It is standard for restaurants in the North Beach NCD.

expected_conditions.condition: Garbage, recycling, and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019 CUA at 526 Columbus required this, and it is standard for eating and drinking uses under San Francisco Department of Public Works guidelines.

expected_conditions.condition: The project sponsor shall appoint a community liaison officer to deal with issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties, and provide the Zoning Administrator and all registered neighborhood groups with the liaison's name, address, and telephone number.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2019 CUA at 526 Columbus required appointment of a community liaison prior to issuance of a building permit. This is a standard condition for uses requiring CUA in neighborhood commercial districts.

filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting and a written Letter of Determination from San Francisco Planning Department.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you propose to expand an existing restaurant at 659 Columbus Ave from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft, that the space has been continuously operated as a restaurant since 1995 and was last expanded in 2010 under CUA case 2009.0798C, and ask whether Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits this expansion and whether any discretionary pathway exists. Request that the planner review the 2010 CUA file and the history of this rule in the North Beach Special Use District. Ask whether the 2010 approval exhausted the right to expand, or whether the rule has been interpreted to allow further enlargement under certain findings.

timeline_cost.notes: No timeline or cost is given because Planning Code §780.3(c)(1)(B) prohibits enlarging an existing restaurant space in the North Beach Special Use District, and the pathway analysis confirms the concept as described is not permitted at this address. The rule lines state that a new restaurant may be approved by Conditional Use only if the Zoning Administrator first finds the new restaurant will not enlarge the space, and the space is to be enlarged from 1,486 sq ft to 2,820 sq ft. The 2010 CUA (case 2009.0798C) approved expansion to over 2,000 sq ft, but no record in the candidate set since 2010 shows a restaurant square-footage expansion approved under this rule, and the current rule text does not provide an exception for existing restaurants. Until Planning confirms in writing whether any discretionary pathway exists, no application should be filed and no cost or timeline for approval can be estimated. If Planning confirms there is no approval path, the only options are to operate within the existing 1,486 sq ft footprint, seek a legislative amendment to the North Beach SUD, or choose a different location.
